notes:
Night 3 results round out the picture nicely:

Report 1 (pre-2023 anomaly): change_history (2 outlier rows out of ~31,099) and compliance_events (1 outlier row out of 9) are clearly negligible noise. data_subject_requests is different: 12 of 60 total rows (20%) predate 2023-01-01 (1 in 2020, 4 in 2021, 7 in 2022) — not negligible. Reassuringly, the 2023-2025 rows sum to exactly 48 (10+23+15), matching the "~48 requests since 2023" figure I've already reported, so that number is internally consistent and unaffected — but I want to quickly check whether any of those 12 pre-2023 rows represent unresolved/backlog risk before I close this out, since they're sitting entirely outside the window I've been reporting on.

Reports 2 and 3 (Feb 2025 pattern + quarterly history) make the spike's character much clearer: 17/11/8 distinct user agents at the three merchants respectively with no single user agent dominating (~25-27% share) — not bot-like; and the quarterly history shows every other quarter at all three merchants sits at a stable 4.8-7.3% fail rate, with Q1 2025 alone spiking to 61-68% — a clean, isolated one-quarter event, not a recurring problem. One more thing worth nailing down before I write the memo: at each merchant individually, ~74-75% of failures cluster in just 3 days — I want to check whether it's the *same* 3 days across all three merchants, which would point to one shared platform-level cause rather than three coincidentally-timed separate issues, and whether access_denied logging was silent specifically on those days (not just the month overall).

This is the last night, so I'm keeping it tight: (1) a quick status check on the 12 pre-2023 DSAR rows, to close out any residual backlog question; (2) a day-by-day breakdown for February 2025 across the three merchants (failed logins per merchant plus access_denied events) to test the shared-cause hypothesis precisely. I'm leaving the third slot unused — I have what I need to write a confident memo and don't have a well-justified third question tonight.
